findings.title: PhusdMinterRepoint (story-064 / YS-12) is incompatible with the live deployed phUSD minter: it ABI-decodes a 7-field StablecoinConfig and calls setMaxMintPerDay, but the live minter has a 4-field config and no cap setter — preview reverts before any mutation, leaving the minter permanently pointed at the evacuated old strategies
findings.sourceContract: lib/phUSD-stable-minter/src/PhusdStableMinter.sol (d6ed115) — declares 7-field struct + setMaxMintPerDay; live 0x435B0A1884bd0fb5667677C9eb0e59425b1477E5 is an OLDER 4-field build
findings.description: The story-064 minter-repoint script was authored against PhusdStableMinter@d6ed115, whose StablecoinConfig is {yieldStrategy, exchangeRate, decimals, enabled, maxMintPerDay, mintedToday, lastMintTimestamp} (7 fields) and which exposes setMaxMintPerDay. The phUSD minter actually deployed at 0x435B..77E5 is an EARLIER version: stablecoinConfigs(token) returns only 4 words {yieldStrategy, exchangeRate(1e18), decimals(18/6), enabled(true)} for both DOLA and USDC (verified by raw cast call: 4x32 bytes), and setMaxMintPerDay(address,uint256) reverts with empty returndata (selector absent). Consequences on a real run: (1) PREFLIGHT reverts — _logLiveConfig (lines 176-183) and _phaseAToken (lines 209-216) destructure a 7-tuple from a 4-word return, so the ABI decoder aborts with empty-data Revert (reproduced: PREVIEW_MODE preview reverts immediately after stablecoinConfigs(DOLA)). (2) Even with a tolerant read, setMaxMintPerDay(token, savedCap) at line 229 reverts (function does not exist). Because the script is UNWIRED and its NatSpec still prescribes --skip-simulation, an operator who hand-broadcasts it tx-by-tx would land setClient + registerStablecoin(token,V2,...) (both selectors exist on the live minter) and then revert on setMaxMintPerDay — leaving the minter mid-repoint, OR if the preflight decode is reached first, broadcast nothing.
findings.impact: YS-12 (the whole point of story-064 — repointing the phUSD minter off the evacuated old strategies onto the new V2 strategies) cannot complete against live mainnet state. If the operator stops at the preflight revert, the minter stays pointed at the OLD DOLA/USDC strategies (0x90ce274b / 0x90af002E), which the YS-swap suite has just evacuated to ~0 principal and which still carry the previewRedeem brick — so every FUTURE phUSD mint for DOLA/USDC deposits into a dead/bricked strategy. If the operator hand-broadcasts past the missing-cap revert, the minter is left half-repointed (config moved to V2 but cap-restore failed) with the registerStablecoin side effects partially applied. Either way the minter's stale principalOf on the old strategy (~13,817 DOLA / ~11k USDC, the run-12 referral amount) is never evacuated. This is an empirical, fork-confirmed broken operation, not a speculative footgun.
findings.evidence: fork: raw stablecoinConfigs(DOLA)=0x...90ce274b.. + 1e18 + 0x12 + 0x01 (4 words); stablecoinConfigs(USDC)=0x...90af002E.. + 1e18 + 0x06 + 0x01 (4 words). setMaxMintPerDay(DOLA,0) -> execution reverted data 0x (selector absent). registerStablecoin(...) -> 0x118cdaa7 (auth revert; selector PRESENT). PREVIEW_MODE forge preview -> [Revert] EvmError immediately after PhusdStableMinter::stablecoinConfigs(DOLA). Live minter codesize 9980, not a proxy.
findings.recommendation: Before running YS-12, reconcile the script against the ACTUAL deployed minter ABI: either (a) read the 4-field config the live minter exposes and drop the maxMintPerDay save/restore + setMaxMintPerDay calls entirely (the live minter has no per-day cap, so there is nothing to preserve), or (b) if a cap is desired, first upgrade/redeploy the minter to the d6ed115 build and re-point references, then run a script matching that build. Add a preflight that probes the live config word-count / a try-decode and aborts with a clear 'minter ABI mismatch — wrong minter version' message instead of a bare decode revert. Wire it as an npm key so it inherits the story-062 preview hard-gate, and remove --skip-simulation from its NatSpec.
findings.reconcile: NEW (story-064). Related to run-12 referral fingerprint (phUSD minter retains ~13,817 DOLA + ~11k USDC) which this script was meant to resolve.

findings.title: Leg1 is still dead-on-arrival against live state: the owner is not an authorized withdrawer on any of the 3 old strategies, so skimSurplus reverts, and the fix wave (story-061) granted withdrawer rights only on the NEW V2 strategies
findings.description: leg1's first mutation is YS_DOLA_OLD.skimSurplus(DOLA, original) (and USDC/USDe). AYieldStrategy.skimSurplus carries onlyAuthorizedWithdrawer; authorizedWithdrawers is a registry distinct from owner, written only by setWithdrawer(onlyOwner). On the fork, authorizedWithdrawers[OWNER]==false on all 3 OLD strategies (the only authorized withdrawer is the SYA). leg1's preflight checks each old strategy's owner() but NOT withdrawer status. story-061 added setWithdrawer(SYA,true) on the new V2 strategies only — it did nothing for the old strategies leg1 actually skims. No suite step grants the broadcasting owner withdrawer rights on the old strategies.
findings.impact: Running the wired migrate:ys-swap-leg1 broadcast reverts at its very first mutating call with 'AYieldStrategy: unauthorized, only authorized withdrawers' (reproduced on the fork) — the migration cannot proceed past leg1 without an out-of-band setWithdrawer on the old strategies. The preview hard-gate (story-062) means this revert also blocks the broadcast, so it is a hard halt, not a silent skip. Availability/operational; no fund loss, owner-recoverable by a one-line setWithdrawer.
findings.evidence: fork: cast call YS_DOLA_OLD authorizedWithdrawers(OWNER)->false; forge broadcast leg1 -> Revert 'AYieldStrategy: unauthorized, only authorized withdrawers' at YS_DOLA_OLD.skimSurplus. After fixup setWithdrawer(OWNER,true) on the 3 old strategies, leg1 completed (skimmed 1.77 USDC + 13.3 USDe, migrated 3 DOLA + 6 USDC stakers).
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit step (in the deploy step or a leg1 pre-broadcast call) that grants the broadcasting owner (or the intended skim caller) setWithdrawer(true) on the 3 old strategies, and add a leg1 preflight require(authorizedWithdrawers[skimCaller]) on each old strategy so the gap fails loudly with guidance rather than at the first skim. Alternatively skim as the SYA (already authorized) if that matches intent.
findings.reconcile: STILL-LIVE carryover of run-12 leg1 Medium 'Leg1 broadcast is dead on arrival: owner is not an authorized withdrawer on any of the 3 old strategies'.

findings.title: story-062 pause coupling: if the YS-swap suite halts after deploy/leg1, the LIVE original staker is left contract-globally paused with no break-glass unpauser — unpause is reachable only through a fully-successful PostMigrationCleanup
findings.description: story-062 deploy now calls setPauser(OWNER)+pause() on BOTH stakers, including the LIVE original. Pause is contract-global, so it also freezes the un-migrated USDe pool for the whole window. The ONLY code that unpauses + restores the original staker's pauser is PostMigrationCleanup (unpause at ~329, setPauser restore at ~342). But cleanup hard-requires ~12 verifications + the solvency invariant (lines 174-304) to pass BEFORE it reaches the unpause; a migration that is incomplete or insolvent cannot reach the unpause. There is no standalone 'unpause/restore' script in script/. So a suite that halts after deploy (e.g. the leg1 withdrawer revert above, or any mid-suite mainnet halt — the exact scenario story-062 was hardening for) leaves the live original staker paused (all stake/withdraw frozen for DOLA, USDC AND the untouched USDe pool) until the operator either completes the entire migration or manually unpauses out-of-band.
findings.impact: User-facing DoS on the live staker (including the unrelated USDe pool) for the duration of any mid-suite halt, with recovery coupled to full migration success rather than an independent break-glass. The in-comment rationale accepts a SHORT window; the finding is that the window is unbounded on failure and has no dedicated reopen path. Owner-recoverable via manual setPauser/unpause, so operational, not fund-loss.
findings.evidence: fork: after deploy broadcast, original staker 0xbce8..079A paused()==true, pauser==OWNER. After full cleanup, paused()==false, pauser restored to 0x7c5A8EeF..85a3. No script/*.s.sol other than PostMigrationCleanup calls unpause() (confirmed by directory scan). cleanup's unpause is downstream of the full verify+solvency gate.
findings.recommendation: Ship a minimal standalone 'EmergencyUnpauseAndRestorePausers' script (reads origPauser/tempPauser from ys-swap-deployments.json, unpauses, restores) that the operator can run if the suite halts, decoupled from the migration-complete verifications. Document the live-pool freeze (esp. the unrelated USDe pool) and its expected duration in the runbook.

findings.title: story-062 cleanup silently SKIPS pauser restoration on the try/catch catch-path (missing/pre-hardening deployments JSON): the live original staker is unpaused but left with the wrong pauser (the deployer EOA) instead of the recorded original pauser
findings.function: run (origPauser/tempPauser try/catch read + gated setPauser restore)
findings.description: cleanup reads origPauser/tempPauser from ys-swap-deployments.json via try/catch (~132-143). On the CATCH path (JSON missing the keys — e.g. a deploy run before the hardening, or a regenerated/partial JSON), origPauserRecorded stays false and the setPauser restore (~342) is gated on that flag, so it is SKIPPED with only a console WARNING. The unpause (gated on paused()) still runs and the post-asserts require !paused, so the staker is reopened — but its pauser remains the deployer EOA (set by the deploy step) rather than the original pauser contract 0x7c5A8EeF..85a3. The post-asserts only check pauser==recorded when *Recorded is true (~373-384), so they pass vacuously on the catch path and do not catch the wrong-pauser end state.
findings.impact: After a catch-path cleanup the emergency-pause authority on the LIVE staker is left as the deployer EOA instead of the intended governance pauser contract — a silent privilege/wiring drift. Not fund-loss and owner-fixable, but it is a non-obvious consequence (the run is reported 'COMPLETE' with a buried warning) — an operational footgun. Low.
findings.evidence: subagent line-trace: catch leaves recorded*=false, setPauser gated on *Recorded -> skipped; post-assert pauser==recorded gated on *Recorded -> vacuously true. Happy-path on the fork DID restore correctly (JSON present), so this only bites the degraded-input path.
findings.recommendation: On the catch path, FAIL LOUDLY (revert) rather than warn-and-continue, OR re-read the pre-pause pauser from an alternate source; and make the post-assert unconditional (require pauser != deployer after restore). At minimum elevate the warning so an operator cannot miss that the pauser was not restored.

findings.title: PhusdMinterRepoint Phase B re-seeds the minter's V2 position with the (possibly below-par) recovered amount and enforces no >= principal solvency floor — a pre-existing autopool shortfall is silently carried into the new strategy
findings.description: Phase B does withdrawAsOwner(minter, owner, p) then recovered = owner balance delta; if recovered < p (autopool below par) it logs a WARNING and does NOT revert (line ~258), then noMintDeposit(V2, token, recovered) re-seeds the new strategy with only the recovered (short) amount. The only post-verify on the re-seeded position is ysTV2.principalOf(token,minter) > 0 (line ~319) — there is NO require(recovered >= p) or principalOf >= prior-liability floor. So a shortfall present at migration time is migrated into the V2 position with no gate.
findings.impact: If the old autopool is below par when YS-12 runs, the minter's V2-backed principal is seeded under its recorded/phUSD liability with no abort. NatSpec frames the shortfall as pre-existing (not migration-caused), which is fair, but the script provides no floor or explicit operator acknowledgement threshold. Low (conditional on a below-par pool; owner-visible via the warning). Note: this is moot until the higher-severity ABI mismatch (NEW-01) is fixed, since the script cannot reach Phase B against the live minter today.
findings.evidence:
static line-trace (script cannot execute against live minter due to the 4-vs-7 field ABI mismatch). recovered

findings.recommendation: Add an explicit operator-set tolerance: require(recovered >= p * minRecoveryBps / 10000) or at minimum a require that the post-reseed principalOf >= the minter's outstanding phUSD liability for that token, so a material shortfall aborts rather than silently migrates under-collateralization.

noFindings.evidence: SYA accounting is strictly per-strategy (strategyTokens used only as decimals/pause key, never an aggregation key); SYA mints no phUSD (it is a consolidator paying out realized skimSurplus output). Two DOLA strategies sum two INDEPENDENT surplus pools; the evacuated old strategy returns 0 (interface guarantees empty client set is a no-op, no revert). On the fork SYA remains an authorized withdrawer on BOTH old and new strategies (so the claim()-revert caveat does NOT apply) and SYA.getTotalYield() over all 5 strategies returns 1.15e16 cleanly. Matches story-061's deliberate deferral of deregistration to YS-12.
